newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures hold gain in light session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures hold gain in light session.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished higher Friday in a light, narrow session, taking cue from the strong daily cash prices due to tight supply and strong energy demand in the Northwest.
Unlike the previous two days, early gains in the May California-Oregon Border (COB) and Palo Verde (PV) futures were trimmed or erased by selling pressure near the close.

May COB settled up 13 cents at $12.06 a megawatt hour (MWh) after traded between $12.00 and $12.15. June COB finished up 15 cents at $12.00. Other COB months ended down five to up two cents from Thursday's settlement.
May PV settled up 30 cents at $15.65 after bouncing in a 25 cent range. June PV finished up 10 cents at $16.55. Deferred PV contracts ended 15 to 35 cents higher.

The colder-than-normal weather in eastern Northwest and the Rockies in recent weeks has slowed the rate of snowmelt and reduced the amount of runoffs into the vast hydroelectric system in the Northwest.
Water spillage for fish migration at the hydroelectric dams on the Snake River was said to have lowered the amount spot hydropower supply in the Northwest.

The absence of offers from Bonneville Power Administration and outages of a number of coal-fired generating units in the West, planned and unplanned, further reduced the amount of generating capacity in the region.
Day-ahead firm, peak power prices at COB for Monday finished at $16.50-17.50 a MWh, up from $16.00-17.00 Thursday, whose those at Palo Verde (PV) jumped to $18.25-19.25 from Thursday's 17.00-18.00.
Despite today's rise, the steady drop in volume showed the market turned cautious awaiting for fresh fundamental news, Brokers and traders said.
"I don't think anyone wants to do anything," said a Houston futures trader.
"This thing has been sitting in the same position. People are like 'Let's see what this weather is going to do'," said an East Coast electricity broker.

In the Northwest, conditions are expected to be generally dry and sunny through Saturday with temperatures averaging near normal. By Sunday and Monday, showers and higher elevation snows would plague the region, dropping back to below normal readings.
In the Southwest, skies will clear and temperatures would slowly moderate toward normal over the weekend. Conditions are expected to be mostly sunny and dry Monday and Tuesday.
NYMEX estimated 208 COB and 198 PV contracts were sold, lower than Thursday's 351 COB and 286 PV lots.
